BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point

The Seller's cover note calls its positions "settled at principal level," "FINAL," "market standard" and "not intended to be re-opened." Under our playbook (secs 0.4 and 6.3), none of that binds us. Those labels are assertions, not authority. Only Amelia Frost's written approval can clear a fallback, and no such approval has been given for any of the positions below. Where the Seller's numbers match a fallback, that does not make the change cleared.

The Seller's own disclosure also contradicts its cover note. The cover says Bluefen is "addressed," but the Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final Bluefen consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions. Riverlark is also unpaid and undischarged (item 3).

## 1. Departures from the playbook

### A. Liability architecture

| Term | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m starting; 20% only with Frost written authority | AUD 1.2m below starting position; fallback not authorised |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher; small claims become non-recoverable |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | Seller recovers nothing until AUD 250k, then only the excess |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | Fallback needs Frost approval, none given |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Fundamental regime abolished |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent | No fraud carve-out |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims" (12.3/13) | Proposed | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Hidden override |

**Reasoning.** The cap, basket and de minimis together mean that for a claim of, say, AUD 300,000 the Seller pays only AUD 50,000 (the excess above the AUD 250,000 basket). Combined with the 18-month window, meaningful recovery becomes improbable. Folding title and capacity into the general regime is the most serious structural problem, because title is the foundation of what we are buying. The fraud carve-out is missing entirely, and the playbook says no one may waive it.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Clause 1.1 and 1.2 of the Disclosure Letter**: the Seller discloses every fact in the whole data room (through 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. This is exactly the blanket deemed disclosure the playbook rejects. Each specific disclosure must be fair and specific.
- **Clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge)**: bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. The playbook requires its deletion, or at most a qualifier tied to named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Clause 8.3 as drafted would hit those too.
- **Item 10 (title)**: the Seller relies on the DD-012 share register as proof of title. The playbook says DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. We need independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.

### C. Specific transactional items

**Bluefen (clauses 3/6.3, Disclosure item 2)**
- The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- The playbook requires effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are both insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Stakes: Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). This is a material customer and the consent conditions in clause 11.3 are unverified.

**Riverlark (clauses 2/7, Disclosure item 3)**
- The Seller proposes a release after Completion, with about AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- The playbook requires a current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is allowed only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
- The Disclosure confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included. Without payment at Completion, we would be taking on AUD 3.2m of secured debt on the company.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow, Disclosure item 5)**
- The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses (plus triggered on-costs) are not in the funds flow. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller," but the funds flow silently excludes them.
- The playbook requires them to be a specific line item or seller-funded. The Disclosure also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply, so the on-cost figure is unquantified.

**Ironquay IP (clause 11.1, Disclosure item 4)**
- The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate." This is narrower than the playbook requires. The playbook says to broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure (cleared payment transfers Project Materials under DD-004 clause 7.3).
- The AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) is not independently verified as unpaid. Neither side should treat it as established either way. We need a receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment.

**Export/privacy incident DD-006 (clause 4.6, Schedule 6, Disclosure item 6)**
- The Seller calls it "not expected to be material."
- The playbook says assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand, in either direction. We should not adopt the Seller's materiality conclusion, nor treat the event as a confirmed breach.
- The Disclosure itself says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown (about 1,240 records) and it is unclear whether anyone accessed the file. We should require preservation of logs, a completed investigation and periodic updates.

**Sandbar renewals (clause "supplier renewals," Disclosure item 8)**
- The Seller calls the three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) "ordinary-course operating costs."
- The playbook says assess them, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. The Disclosure says whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course is not stated. We should not accept the "ordinary course" label until the timing and scope are assessed.

**Tax and IP (cover note)**
- The Seller says the tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." This contradicts the playbook: Tax/IP terms remain open and must be kept separate from the general regime. We should not assume unlimited liability, and we should not accept that anything is resolved.

**Items not covered by the playbook but flagged by the Disclosure**
- **Office lease (item 7)**: a notification obligation exists, but the Disclosure does not say whether landlord consent to the share sale is needed. Confirm.
- **Mossvale (item 9)**: assignment restriction, but no statement that Mossvale consent is needed for a share sale. Confirm.

## 2. What to push back on

1. Reject the "FINAL / settled / market standard" framing in writing. Ask the Seller to identify any Frost-authorised position they rely on. None exists.
2. Restore a 25% / AUD 6.0m general cap. Do not accept AUD 4.8m without Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. Restore a first-dollar basket of AUD 50,000 and a de minimis of AUD 5,000.
4. Restore a 24-month general claims period.
5. Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limits, including the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
7. Delete clauses 1.1 and 1.2 of the Disclosure Letter. Require specific fair disclosure only.
8. Delete clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge), or limit any qualifier to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and carve out title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.
9. Bluefen: require effective written consent and evidence the conditions are satisfied before Completion, not consent-on-delivery.
10. Riverlark: payout from Completion funds, with security releases effective at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
11. Funds flow: itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs, or require the Seller to fund them.
12. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity, keeping the SOW3 cure. Require a receipt or confirmatory assignment.
13. Export incident: require log preservation, completion of the investigation and regular updates. Do not accept "not material."
14. Sandbar: assess the renewals. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
15. Tax and IP: keep open and separate. Do not accept "settled."
16. Title: require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. The DD-012 register is not enough.
17. Obtain written confirmation on the office lease and Mossvale consent requirements.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

The Seller's package departs from the playbook on nearly every material term: caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, the abolition of a separate title regime, the missing fraud carve-out, blanket disclosure and buyer knowledge, and the consent and payoff mechanics for Bluefen and Riverlark. It also omits the bonuses from the funds flow and asserts "settled" positions that are not settled. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note on Bluefen and Riverlark.

Recommended approach: reject the package as drafted, return a mark-up restoring playbook positions on each point above, and require Completion conditions on Bluefen consent and Riverlark payout. Do not concede any fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft. Before the mark-up goes out, NSW counsel should confirm that the fraud carve-out and the separate title regime are drafted to be enforceable. The AUD 180,000 Ironquay figure, the on-costs on the bonuses and the Sandbar timing all need independent verification.
